series1_api_core.note: Observed points only — the bucket is read at check time, not sampled continuously. Dashed connectors span unobserved gaps; they are not measurements. Buckets stay separate (see buckets) — this line is the PAT user bucket only, never merged with installation or GraphQL spend. model.principle: Owner principle (2026-10-29 19:10 PT, via cadence lane): the target line is NOT a survival ceiling — it is the replenishment flow line (limit / window, phase-aligned to reset epochs), with cumulative use reaching ~100% exactly at replenishment.
model.ideal: remaining declines linearly from the limit at window start to 0 exactly at the reset epoch — a diagonal burn-down pacing to zero-at-reset

faults.below_line: actual under the flow line = burn ahead of pace -> burst fault: early death before the reset epoch
faults.above_line: actual over the flow line late in the window = burn behind pace -> flat fault: quota wasted at replenishment

worked.read: burst fault — bucket dead ~10 min before its reset epoch
~1.8x pace in the new window (used 1770 vs ~988 ideal) — burst fault forming

model.note: Reset epochs drift seconds per window (observed resets 01:42:09Z -> 02:42:19Z); the line is phase-aligned to the anchor epoch, not to the clock hour.

annotations.text: PAT wall ↔ multi-lane polling in hot merge hours (quota pack: tier1 steward + viz + quota-convergence publish attempts active). Per-consumer attribution NOT ESTABLISHED — GitHub exposes none to a PAT (cadence lane). Lesson of record: poll sparingly, batch reads, head-SHA check-runs.
Fresh window: 42 core calls fleet-wide in 77s (~1900/h baseline pace before spikes) — cadence lane timeline, rate-limit record PR #2321/#2322.

Incident 2 (rate-limit lane record): the full 5000-call window burned in ~25 min (11:41:45Z–~12:06Z); the earlier ~1452-call figure was only the forwarding lane's 11:56Z–12:06Z segment. Per-consumer attribution NOT ESTABLISHED.

Feed-collect burst ↔ delphi-gate workflow_run storm: 143 runs / 25 min, each firing UNTHROTTLED delphi-rfp-feed-collect (~30–80 installation-token calls); reviewer map crossed 24h staleness mid-storm → orchestrator completions launched ~750-call reviewer-metrics collects on the PAT token. Fixed by PR #2341 (merged 97938a583f50): retry ×4 + 15-min freshness gate loop breaker; 3 workflows re-enabled green.
QAC-007 (PR #2323): pat_publish derived-reserve preflight enacted — publish defers when remaining < planned calls + limit/10, so lanes stop draining the shared bucket into walls.
Vercel cap-trip 2026-10-20 ↔ dashboard deploy bursts (tribute-vercel-prod promotions; registry notes API undercounts enforcement ≥13). OpenRouter free daily cap exhausted the same day.

Burn shape correction (convergence, verified from reset epochs): NO instant re-exhaustion — the new window opened at the 01:42:09Z reset and drained on a sustained ~120–160 calls/min ramp (4999 @01:43Z viz preflight → 4645 @~01:45Z → 3230 @~01:54Z, used 1770). A 5000 bucket dies in ~30–40 min of storm and stays dead until the hourly reset; graph walls as ramps, not spikes. Consistent with the quota lane's firsthand ~150/min, ~32-min burn on 2026-10-29.

Model correction (owner principle via cadence lane, 2026-10-29 19:10 PT): the green line is the replenishment FLOW line — limit/window phased to reset epochs, ideal = diagonal to zero-at-reset. Deviations are faults both ways: below = burst (early death; the 01:32Z wall sat at 0 with ~846 ideal remaining), above late = flat (wasted quota). At 01:54Z the new window burned ~1.8x pace — a burst fault forming, visible against the line.

series6_self_counts.title: Self-counted usage - fleet tally of record
series6_self_counts.source: ops/quota/self-counts.json (quota-self-counts/v1) - tallied by scripts/quota_self_counts.py from committed sources; this section is its pack copy, carried verbatim
series6_self_counts.note: Self-counted tallies of recorded events, method-stamped by the tally itself. Not provider readings; heuristics cite this tally, never re-tally.
series6_self_counts.method: self-count: tallies of the fleet's own recorded events from committed sources (owner ruling 2026-11-03). Not provider readings; not estimates. Provider readings govern where present; these counts govern where readings are null.
coverage_notes: PAT helper spend logs (spend.jsonl beside the helper) are VM-local and not committed - PAT call volume is NOT tallied here; its wall events are (rate-limit register). Export of the spend log is the follow-up that closes this blind spot.
Provider-side token/$ consumption is visible only where a dispatch was stamped (routed-dispatch + nested-family carriers); unstamped consumption is not counted and not estimated.
Dispatch counts are per provider (dispatch records name provider+model, not registry service id); the planner rolls them up to pools by provider.
